a.a-star.summary: A best-first search that expands vertices in order of the sum of the cost from the start, g, and an admissible heuristic estimate of the cost to the goal, h.
a.aa-tree.summary: A red-black tree variant that simplifies implementation by allowing red nodes only as right children.
a.adaboost.summary: A boosting method that combines weak classifiers sequentially, increasing the weights of the samples misclassified by the previous weak classifier.
a.adagrad.summary: An adaptive learning-rate method that divides the learning rate by each coordinate's accumulated sum of squared gradients, giving larger updates to rarely occurring features.
a.adam.summary: An adaptive optimizer that sets per-coordinate step sizes from bias-corrected exponential moving averages of the first and second moments of the gradient.
a.adamw.summary: A fix to Adam that decouples weight decay from the adaptive gradient update so that it behaves differently from L2 regularization.
a.additive-attention.summary: An attention mechanism that, at each decoder step, learns alignment weights over the encoder hidden states to form a context vector.
a.aes.summary: A substitution–permutation network block cipher with a 128-bit block and 128/192/256-bit keys. It was adopted as a US federal standard in 2001.
a.aho-corasick.summary: An algorithm that finds multiple patterns in a single pass over the text using an automaton formed by adding failure links to a trie of the pattern set.
a.alexnet.summary: A deep convolutional neural network that combined ReLU, dropout, and GPU training to win ImageNet 2012 by a large margin.
a.alpha-beta.o0.note: Correctness and efficiency analyzed by Knuth and Moore (1975)
a.alpha-beta.summary: A technique that obtains the same result as minimax with less search by pruning branches outside the current best-value window (α, β).
a.ans.summary: An entropy coding method that accumulates symbols into a single integer state according to their probabilities, achieving arithmetic-coding-level compression at Huffman-level speed.
a.argon2.summary: A password hash built on a BLAKE2b-based memory-hard function that raises the cost of GPU and ASIC attacks. It is the winner of the Password Hashing Competition.
a.arithmetic-coding.summary: A coding method that narrows the entire message down to a single real subinterval of [0,1), approaching the entropy without the constraint of an integer number of bits per symbol.
a.avl-tree.summary: The first self-balancing binary search tree, which keeps the height difference between the two subtrees of every node at most 1.
a.b-tree.o0.note: First released as a 1970 Boeing research laboratory report
a.b-tree.summary: A balanced multiway search tree that keeps its height low by storing multiple keys and children in each node. It is the standard for disk-based indexes.
a.backpropagation.o0.note: First description of reverse-mode automatic differentiation
a.backpropagation.o0.venue: University of Helsinki master's thesis (in Finnish)
a.backpropagation.summary: A method that applies the chain rule from the output layer toward the input layer to compute the gradients of all weights in a neural network in a single backward pass.
a.bagging.summary: An ensemble method that reduces variance by training a model on each bootstrap sample and combining their predictions by averaging or voting.
a.batch-norm.summary: A technique that stabilizes training by normalizing layer inputs with minibatch statistics and then applying a learnable scale and shift.
a.baum-welch.summary: A maximum-likelihood algorithm that iteratively estimates the parameters of a hidden Markov model using forward and backward probabilities.
a.bcrypt.summary: A password hash that slows brute-force attacks by repeating the Blowfish key setup a number of times set by a cost factor (Eksblowfish).
a.bellman-ford.summary: An algorithm that relaxes every edge V−1 times to compute single-source shortest paths with negative weights allowed, and detects negative cycles.
a.bentley-ottmann.summary: An algorithm that reports all k intersection points among line segments in O((n + k) log n) using a sweep line and an event queue.
a.bert.summary: A bidirectional representation model that pretrains a Transformer encoder with masked language modeling and next sentence prediction.
a.bezier-curve.o0.title: Citroën internal technical report
a.bezier-curve.o1.title: Renault UNISURF surface design system
a.bezier-curve.summary: A method for defining and evaluating smooth curves by repeated linear interpolation of control points. It was devised independently in automobile body design.
a.bfs.o0.title: Connected-component search in the Plankalkül dissertation manuscript
a.bfs.summary: A graph traversal that uses a queue to visit vertices in order of their distance from the start vertex. It finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
a.binary-heap.summary: A priority queue that stores a complete binary tree in an array and keeps every parent greater than or equal to its children.
a.binary-insertion-sort.o0.title: Mention of binary insertion in the Moore School Lectures
a.binary-insertion-sort.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3
a.binary-insertion-sort.summary: An insertion sort that finds the insertion position by binary search, reducing the number of comparisons to O(n log n).
a.binary-search.o0.note: The form that works for all n is due to D. H. Lehmer (1960)
a.binary-search.o0.title: Mention of binary search in the Moore School Lectures
a.binary-search.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3 §6.2.1
a.binary-search.summary: A search that halves the search interval of a sorted array at each step, finding an element in O(log n).
a.binomial-heap.summary: A data structure that represents a priority queue as a forest of binomial trees, supporting the merging of two heaps in O(log n).
a.bitonic-sort.summary: A sorting network that repeatedly merges bitonic sequences. Its comparison order is independent of the input, making it well suited to parallel hardware.
a.blake.summary: A hash that uses the ChaCha core operation as its compression function. It was a finalist in the SHA-3 competition.
a.blake2.summary: A hash that reduces the number of rounds in BLAKE and adds a parameter block, making it faster than MD5.
a.blake3.summary: A hash and XOF that parallelizes the BLAKE2s compression function in a Merkle tree mode.
a.blast.summary: A heuristic for searching large sequence databases that approximates local alignment by extending short word matches used as seeds.
a.blinn-phong.summary: An illumination model that approximates specular reflection using the halfway vector instead of the Phong model's reflection vector. It was the default lighting in fixed-function GPU pipelines.
a.bloom-filter.summary: A probabilistic data structure that marks a bit array with multiple hashes to test set membership with no false negatives and a tolerated rate of false positives.
a.blowfish.summary: A Feistel cipher with a 64-bit block that uses key-dependent S-boxes. Its key setup is deliberately expensive.
a.bluestein-fft.summary: An algorithm that computes a DFT of arbitrary length with power-of-two FFTs by recasting it as a convolution with a chirp signal.
a.boids.summary: A distributed behavioral model that reproduces flocking behavior with only three rules: separation, alignment, and cohesion.
a.boruvka.summary: The first minimum spanning tree algorithm, which merges components by simultaneously adding the cheapest outgoing edge of each component.
a.bowyer-watson.summary: A Delaunay triangulation algorithm that inserts points one at a time, deleting the triangles whose circumcircle contains the new point and retriangulating the resulting cavity.
a.boyer-moore.summary: A string search that compares the pattern from right to left and skips ahead by large amounts using the bad-character and good-suffix rules.
a.bresenham-circle.summary: An algorithm that rasterizes a circle using only integer arithmetic, via octant symmetry and incremental error decisions.
a.bresenham-line.summary: An algorithm that draws a line on a raster grid using only integer addition and an error term.
a.brotli.o0.note: Originally developed by Google in 2013 for WOFF 2.0
a.brotli.summary: A web compression format that combines LZ77, Huffman coding, second-order context modeling, and a built-in static dictionary.
a.bst.summary: A binary tree that places smaller keys in the left subtree and larger keys in the right subtree. It was devised independently by several researchers around 1960.
a.bwt.summary: A reversible transform that sorts all rotations of a string and takes the last column. Grouping identical characters together improves the compression ratio.
a.bzip2.summary: A block-sorting compressor that applies BWT, MTF, run-length encoding, and Huffman coding in sequence.
a.c4-5.summary: A successor to ID3 for building decision trees that adds the gain ratio, splits on continuous attributes, handling of missing values, and pruning.
a.cart.summary: Classification and regression trees that make binary splits by Gini impurity or squared error and apply cost-complexity pruning.
a.catmull-clark.summary: An algorithm that subdivides polygon meshes of arbitrary topology into smooth surfaces by systematically adding face, edge, and vertex points.
a.chacha.summary: A stream cipher that modifies the Salsa20 quarter-round to increase diffusion per round.
a.chacha20-poly1305.summary: An AEAD construction that combines ChaCha20 encryption with Poly1305 authentication. It is one of the mandatory cipher suites of TLS 1.3.
a.chan-hull.summary: An O(n log h) convex hull algorithm that runs Graham scan on small groups and then performs a Jarvis march over the group hulls.
a.cheney.summary: An algorithm that performs copying GC without recursion or an auxiliary stack by using the new semispace itself as the breadth-first search queue.
a.chord.summary: A distributed hash table protocol that provides O(log n)-hop lookups using finger tables on a consistent hashing ring.
a.consistent-hashing.summary: A distributed hashing scheme that places nodes and keys on the same hash ring so that only about 1/n of the keys move when nodes are added or removed.
a.coppersmith-winograd.summary: An algorithm that lowered the matrix multiplication exponent to 2.376 using a laser method that exploits arithmetic progression structure.
a.copying-gc.summary: A garbage collector that reclaims memory without fragmentation by copying and compacting live objects into the other semispace.
a.count-min-sketch.summary: A sketch that approximates the frequencies of stream elements, erring toward overestimation, by taking the minimum of counters across multiple hash rows.
a.counting-bloom-filter.summary: An extension of the Bloom filter that uses counters instead of bits to support element deletion.
a.counting-sort.summary: A non-comparison sort that counts the occurrences of each key value and determines positions from prefix sums. It runs in O(n + k) for a key range k.
a.cuckoo-filter.summary: An approximate set-membership structure that stores fingerprints in a cuckoo hash table and supports deletion.
a.cuckoo-hashing.summary: A hashing scheme that gives each key two candidate positions and, on a collision, evicts the existing key to its other candidate, guaranteeing worst-case O(1) lookups.
a.cyk.o0.venue: Air Force Cambridge Research Lab technical report
a.cyk.summary: An O(n³) parsing algorithm for grammars in Chomsky normal form that fills a table with the nonterminals that can generate each substring.
a.d-star.summary: A dynamic A* that incrementally replans paths when edge costs change in a partially known environment.
a.deflate.o0.title: The Deflate method of PKZIP 2.0
a.deflate.summary: A format that further compresses the output of LZ77 match finding with Huffman codes. It underlies zip, gzip, and PNG.
a.des.summary: A block cipher with a 56-bit key and a 16-round Feistel structure. It became a US federal standard in 1977.
a.dfs.o0.note: A method devised in the 19th century, recorded by Lucas
a.dfs.o0.title: Trémaux's maze-solving method
a.dfs.o0.venue: Recorded in Édouard Lucas, Récréations mathématiques Vol. 1
a.dfs.summary: A graph traversal that goes as deep as possible before backtracking. It is the backbone of many graph algorithms.
a.diffie-hellman.summary: A public-key protocol that relies on the hardness of the discrete logarithm problem to let two parties agree on a shared secret over an eavesdropped channel.
a.dijkstra.summary: A single-source shortest-path algorithm for graphs with nonnegative weights that grows the set of vertices with finalized shortest distances one vertex at a time.
a.dinic.summary: An algorithm that computes maximum flow in O(V²E) by repeatedly building level graphs and blocking flows.
a.dot-product-attention.summary: Global and local attention that computes alignment scores as the dot product of the decoder state and the encoder states.
a.dropout.summary: A regularization technique that randomly disables neurons during training and scales the weights at inference to prevent co-adaptation.
a.dsa.summary: A US federal standard signature scheme that reduces signature size by restricting ElGamal signatures to a prime-order subgroup.
a.dual-pivot-quicksort.o0.title: Dual-Pivot Quicksort proposal
a.dual-pivot-quicksort.summary: A quicksort variant that uses two pivots to partition the array into three segments. It was adopted as Java 7's sort for arrays of primitive types.
a.earley.summary: An algorithm that parses arbitrary context-free grammars in O(n³), and unambiguous grammars in O(n²), by maintaining state sets as a chart.
a.ecc.summary: Public-key cryptography that uses the discrete logarithm problem in the group of points on an elliptic curve over a finite field, achieving the same security with shorter keys.
a.ecdsa.o0.title: Proposed in response to the NIST DSS proposal
a.ecdsa.summary: A digital signature scheme that carries DSA over to elliptic curve groups.
a.eddsa.summary: A variant of the Schnorr signature over twisted Edwards curves. Deterministic nonces rule out randomness failures entirely.
a.edmonds-karp.summary: A maximum-flow algorithm that guarantees O(VE²) time by choosing augmenting paths in Ford–Fulkerson as BFS shortest paths.
a.elgamal.summary: A discrete-logarithm-based public-key scheme that extends Diffie–Hellman key agreement to encryption and signatures.
a.em.summary: A general algorithm that finds maximum-likelihood estimates from incomplete data by alternating between computing the posterior expectations of latent variables (E) and maximizing over the parameters (M).
a.euclidean-algorithm.summary: An algorithm that computes the greatest common divisor of two integers by repeatedly replacing the larger number with its remainder modulo the smaller.
a.exponential-search.summary: A search for unbounded arrays that doubles the search range to find an upper bound and then performs binary search within it.
a.fenwick-tree.summary: An array-based tree that partitions ranges by the lowest set bit to answer prefix-sum queries and perform point updates in O(log n).
a.fft.o0.note: Origin confirmed by Heideman, Johnson, and Burrus (1984)
a.fft.o0.venue: Unpublished manuscript (included in the 1866 collected works)
a.fft.summary: An algorithm that computes the discrete Fourier transform of length N in O(N log N) by recursively decomposing it into smaller transforms.
a.fibonacci-heap.summary: A heap that defers work to support decrease-key in amortized O(1) time. It improved the theoretical bounds of Dijkstra's and Prim's algorithms.
a.flajolet-martin.summary: A probabilistic counting method that approximates the number of distinct elements from the trailing zero-bit patterns of hash values.
a.flash-attention-2.summary: An improved FlashAttention that raises GPU utilization by reducing non-matmul operations and parallelizing across the sequence dimension as well.
a.flash-attention.summary: An exact attention implementation that computes attention tile by tile in SRAM and combines the tiles with an online softmax, reducing HBM reads and writes.
a.floyd-warshall.summary: An algorithm that computes all-pairs shortest paths by O(V³) dynamic programming, admitting intermediate vertices one at a time.
a.fm-index.summary: A full-text index that combines the BWT with a rank-query structure to count pattern occurrences, while compressed, in time proportional to the pattern length.
a.ford-fulkerson.summary: A maximum-flow method that sends flow along each augmenting path it finds in the residual graph.
a.fortune.summary: An algorithm that constructs the Voronoi diagram in O(n log n) using a sweep line and a parabolic beach line.
a.furer.summary: An integer multiplication algorithm that reduces the log log n factor of Schönhage–Strassen to 2^O(log* n) using an FFT over a ring with complex roots of unity.
a.generational-gc.summary: A garbage collector that, based on the hypothesis that most objects die young, collects the young generation frequently and the old generation rarely.
a.gibbs-sampling.summary: An MCMC method that samples each variable in turn from its conditional distribution with all other variables held fixed.
a.gjk.summary: An algorithm that computes the distance and collision between two convex bodies by iteratively testing, with simplices, whether their Minkowski difference contains the origin.
a.gouraud-shading.summary: A technique that shades curved surfaces smoothly by linearly interpolating intensities computed at the vertices across the polygon interior.
a.gpt.summary: A language model that generatively pretrains a Transformer decoder on next-token prediction and then fine-tunes it for each task.
a.gradient-boosting.summary: Boosting by gradient descent in function space, sequentially fitting weak learners to the negative gradient (pseudo-residuals) of the loss function and adding them.
a.gradient-descent.summary: An optimization method that finds a minimum by repeatedly moving in the direction opposite to the gradient of the objective function.
a.graham-scan.summary: An algorithm that computes the convex hull in O(n log n) by sorting points by polar angle about the lowest point and then using a stack to eliminate right turns.
a.grouped-query-attention.summary: A generalization between multi-head and multi-query attention that groups query heads and shares keys and values within each group.
a.gru.summary: A simplified recurrent unit that learns long-term dependencies comparably to LSTM using only two gates, update and reset.
a.harvey-van-der-hoeven.summary: An algorithm that multiplies integers in O(n log n) using multidimensional FFT techniques, attaining the bound of a long-standing conjecture.
a.hash-chaining.o0.title: IBM internal memo (chained hashing)
a.hash-chaining.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3 §6.4
a.hash-chaining.summary: A hash table that selects a bucket with a hash function and links colliding keys in a linked list.
a.heapsort.o0.note: In the same year, R. W. Floyd improved heap construction in Algorithm 245 Treesort 3
a.heapsort.summary: An in-place sort that builds a binary heap and repeatedly extracts the maximum. It runs in O(n log n) worst-case time.
a.hits.summary: A link analysis algorithm that computes hub and authority scores through mutually reinforcing iteration.
a.hmac.summary: A construction that builds a message authentication code by wrapping a hash function twice, with an inner and an outer key.
a.horspool.summary: A practical string search that simplifies Boyer–Moore by keeping only the bad-character rule.
a.huffman.summary: A greedy algorithm that builds a prefix code of minimum average code length by repeatedly merging the two least frequent symbols.
a.hungarian.summary: An algorithm based on the theorems of Kőnig and Egerváry that solves minimum-cost perfect matching in bipartite graphs (the assignment problem) in polynomial time.
a.hunt-szymanski.summary: An algorithm that computes the longest common subsequence quickly on inputs with few matches by processing only pairs of matching positions.
a.hyperloglog-pp.summary: An improved HyperLogLog that adds 64-bit hashes, bias correction for small cardinalities, and a sparse representation.
a.hyperloglog.summary: A cardinality estimation algorithm that combines LogLog registers with a harmonic mean to reduce the standard error.
a.id3.summary: An algorithm that builds a decision tree by recursively splitting each node on the attribute with the highest information gain.
a.ida-star.summary: A search that repeats depth-first search with a gradually increasing bound on f = g + h, achieving the optimality of A* with linear memory.
a.improved-perlin-noise.summary: A revision of the original Perlin noise that reduces its artifacts using a quintic interpolation function and a fixed set of gradients.
a.insertion-sort.summary: A sort that inserts elements one at a time into the sorted prefix. It is fast on nearly sorted input and serves as the small-subarray stage of many hybrid sorts.
a.interpolation-search.summary: A search that assumes a distribution of key values and chooses the next probe position by linear interpolation. It takes O(log log n) on average for uniformly distributed keys.
a.introsort.summary: A hybrid sort that starts with quicksort and switches to heapsort when the recursion depth exceeds a limit, guaranteeing O(n log n) worst-case time.
a.jarvis-march.summary: An output-sensitive convex hull algorithm that, from the current vertex, selects as the next vertex the point with all other points on one side.
a.johnson.summary: An all-pairs shortest-path algorithm that computes vertex potentials with Bellman–Ford, reweights the edges to be nonnegative, and then runs Dijkstra's algorithm from every vertex.
a.jump-consistent-hash.summary: A hash that consistently assigns keys to n buckets with a few lines of arithmetic and no storage.
a.jump-point-search.summary: A technique that speeds up A* on uniform-cost grids by pruning symmetric paths and expanding only jump points.
a.k-means-pp.summary: A k-means initialization that picks each subsequent initial center with probability proportional to its squared distance from the existing centers, guaranteeing an O(log k) approximation.
a.k-means.o1.venue: Bell Labs technical memo (published in IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 28(2), 1982)
a.k-means.summary: A clustering method that repeatedly assigns each point to its nearest center and moves each center to the mean of its assigned points.
a.karatsuba.summary: The first subquadratic multiplication algorithm, which reduces the product of two n-digit numbers to three n/2-digit products and runs in O(n^1.585).
a.karmarkar.summary: A polynomial-time interior-point method for linear programming that is efficient in practice, using projective transformations and an interior path.
a.kd-tree.summary: A multidimensional binary search tree that bisects space along alternating coordinate axes. It is used for nearest-neighbor and range queries.
a.kmp.o1.note: Joint publication including Knuth's independent discovery
a.kmp.summary: A string search that uses a failure function to reuse information about already matched prefixes, finding a pattern in O(n + m) without backing up in the text.
a.kosaraju-scc.o0.title: Unpublished (circulated via Aho, Hopcroft, and Ullman's lecture materials)
a.kosaraju-scc.summary: An algorithm that finds strongly connected components by running DFS twice, once on the original graph and once on its transpose.
a.kruskal.summary: A minimum spanning tree algorithm that scans edges in order of weight and accepts only those that do not create a cycle.
a.lalr.summary: A parsing method that merges LR(1) states with identical cores to reduce table size to that of LR(0). It is used by yacc and bison.
a.lamport-clock.summary: A technique that uses a logical clock, increasing monotonically with each event, to produce a total order consistent with the causal (happened-before) order in a distributed system.
a.layer-norm.summary: A normalization method that uses statistics over all hidden units of a single sample instead of the batch, so it works independently of batch size.
a.lcg.o0.venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Symposium on Large-Scale Digital Calculating Machinery (published 1951)
a.lcg.summary: A generator that produces pseudorandom numbers via the recurrence x ← (a·x + c) mod m.
a.lenet.summary: A convolutional neural network that recognized handwritten ZIP codes by training convolution and subsampling layers end to end with backpropagation.
a.levenshtein-distance.summary: An edit distance that defines the difference between two strings as the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and substitutions.
a.lightgbm.summary: Gradient boosting accelerated by Gradient-based One-Side Sampling (GOSS) and Exclusive Feature Bundling (EFB).
a.linear-probing.o0.title: Open-addressing hashing in the IBM 701 assembler
a.linear-probing.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3 §6.4
a.linear-probing.summary: An open-addressing hash table that examines the next slot sequentially on a collision.
a.linear-sieve.summary: A sieve that finds primes in O(n) by crossing out each composite exactly once, via its smallest prime factor.
a.loglog.summary: An algorithm that estimates the number of distinct elements in log-log memory by recording the maximum run of leading zeros of hashes in multiple registers.
a.lora.summary: A method that freezes the pretrained weights and trains only a product of low-rank matrices, greatly reducing the number of fine-tuning parameters.
a.lr-parsing.summary: A bottom-up parsing method that reads input left to right using a stack and a state automaton, producing a rightmost derivation in reverse.
a.lsm-tree.summary: An index that increases write throughput by accumulating writes in an in-memory component and sequentially merging them into sorted on-disk components.
a.lstm.o0.note: Forget gate added by Gers et al. (2000)
a.lstm.summary: An architecture that controls a cell state with input, forget, and output gates, mitigating the vanishing gradient problem in recurrent neural networks.
a.lucifer.summary: An early IBM block cipher using a Feistel structure. It is the predecessor of DES.
a.lz4.summary: A compression method that maximizes decompression speed by using only byte-aligned LZ77 sequences without entropy coding.
a.lz77.summary: A dictionary compression method that references the longest match within a sliding window of previously seen data as a (distance, length) pair.
a.lz78.summary: A dictionary compression method that explicitly grows its dictionary by parsing the input into an existing dictionary entry plus one character.
a.lzma.o0.title: LZMA compression in 7-Zip
a.lzma.summary: A compression method that combines LZ77 matching over a large dictionary with context-model-based range coding. It is the core of the 7z and xz formats.
a.lzss.summary: A variant that reduces the waste in LZ77 by emitting literals as-is when a match is shorter than the cost of a reference.
a.lzw.summary: A dictionary compression method that eliminates the explicit character output of LZ78 by initializing the dictionary with all single characters. It was used in GIF and Unix compress.
a.manacher.summary: An algorithm that finds the longest palindrome around every center in linear time by reusing the symmetry of previously computed palindrome radii.
a.marching-cubes.summary: An algorithm that extracts a surface mesh by triangulating each cube of a 3D grid using a table of the patterns in which the isosurface passes through it.
a.mark-sweep.summary: A tracing garbage collector that marks objects reachable from the roots and then reclaims unmarked objects.
a.mccreight-algorithm.summary: An algorithm that uses suffix links to build a suffix tree, starting from the longest suffix, in linear time and with little memory.
a.mcts.summary: A game tree search that accumulates the results of random playouts in a tree to progressively search promising moves more deeply.
a.md4.summary: A hash function that produces a 128-bit digest with three rounds of 32-bit word operations. It became the template for the later MD5 and SHA family designs.
a.md5.summary: A 128-bit hash that strengthens MD4 with a fourth round and unique additive constants. Collision attacks now make it unsuitable for security purposes.
a.median-of-medians.summary: An algorithm that solves the selection problem in worst-case linear time by using the median of the medians of groups of five as the pivot.
a.merge-sort.o0.title: Merge sort program for the EDVAC (unpublished manuscript)
a.merge-sort.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3
a.merge-sort.summary: A divide-and-conquer sort that splits the array in half, sorts each half, and merges them in linear time. It runs in O(n log n) worst-case time and is stable.
a.merkle-damgard.summary: A construction that builds a collision-resistant hash by chaining a fixed-length compression function over padded blocks.
a.merkle-tree.o0.note: Publicly described in the CRYPTO ’87 paper "A Digital Signature Based on a Conventional Encryption Function"
a.merkle-tree.summary: A tree in which each parent is the hash of its children's hashes. A single root hash verifies the integrity of large volumes of data.
a.mersenne-twister.summary: A twisted GFSR pseudorandom number generator whose period is the Mersenne prime 2^19937−1.
a.metropolis-hastings.summary: A generalization of the Metropolis algorithm that corrects the acceptance probability to allow asymmetric proposal distributions.
a.metropolis.summary: A sampling method that constructs a Markov chain with the Boltzmann distribution as its stationary distribution by accepting proposed states with a probability determined by the energy difference.
a.minimax.o0.note: Theoretical basis is von Neumann's 1928 minimax theorem
a.minimax.summary: A search that assumes the opponent plays optimally and alternately takes the maximum and minimum evaluation at each move of the game tree.
a.mipmapping.summary: A texture filtering technique that precomputes a pyramid of textures, each at half the previous resolution, to reduce aliasing under minification.
a.momentum.summary: Gradient descent that accumulates previous update directions like inertia, damping oscillations across ravines and accelerating convergence.
a.monotone-chain.summary: A variant of Graham scan that sorts points by x-coordinate and scans the upper and lower hulls separately.
a.monte-carlo.o0.note: Devised around 1946 at Los Alamos together with Ulam and von Neumann
a.monte-carlo.summary: A method that approximates quantities such as integrals and expected values by averaging random samples.
a.move-to-front.summary: A transform that outputs each symbol's position in a list and moves the most recently used symbol to the front, turning local repetitions into small numbers.
a.multi-query-attention.summary: Attention in which all heads share a single key and value projection, reducing memory bandwidth during decoding.
a.myers-diff.summary: A diff algorithm that finds a shortest edit script in O(ND) by advancing the furthest-reaching point on each diagonal of the edit graph. It is the default algorithm of git diff.
a.needleman-wunsch.summary: An algorithm that finds an optimal global alignment of two biological sequences by dynamic programming.
a.neocognitron.summary: A hierarchical neural network that alternates layers of simple and complex cells to recognize patterns robustly under positional shifts. It is the prototype of the CNN.
a.nesterov.summary: An accelerated gradient method that evaluates the gradient at the point reached by a momentum look-ahead step, guaranteeing O(1/k²) convergence on convex problems.
a.newton-method.summary: A root-finding method that iteratively updates the estimate to the x-intercept of the tangent line, converging quadratically near a simple root.
a.odd-even-merge-sort.summary: A sorting network that merges odd and even positions separately, using O(n log² n) comparators.
a.pagerank.summary: An algorithm that ranks the importance of web documents by the stationary distribution of a random surfer on the link structure.
a.pairing-heap.summary: A self-adjusting heap built from a single multiway tree and pairwise merging that is simple to implement and performs well in practice.
a.path-tracing.summary: A technique that computes global illumination by solving the rendering equation via Monte Carlo integration over random path samples.
a.patricia-trie.summary: A trie that compresses nodes with only one child and stores only the branching bits.
a.paxos.summary: A protocol that reaches consensus on a single value despite non-Byzantine failures through two phases of majority-quorum voting.
a.pbkdf2.summary: A function that derives a key from a password by repeatedly applying a pseudorandom function (typically HMAC).
a.pca.summary: A linear transformation that reduces dimensionality by rotating the data onto orthogonal axes ordered by decreasing variance.
a.pcg.o0.venue: Harvey Mudd College Technical Report HMC-CS-2014-0905
a.pcg.summary: A family of generators that applies a state-dependent permutation as the output function on an LCG state, achieving high statistical quality with a small state.
a.pdqsort.o0.note: C++ implementation released before the paper; adopted by the Rust and Go standard libraries
a.pdqsort.summary: An unstable hybrid sort that extends introsort to detect sorted, reverse-sorted, and repeated patterns, and shuffles pivots on adversarial inputs.
a.perceptron.summary: A learning rule for a linear classifier that classifies by whether a weighted sum exceeds a threshold and, on a misclassification, adjusts the weights in the direction of the input.
a.perlin-noise.summary: A gradient noise that produces natural-looking textures by smoothly interpolating random gradients at lattice points.
a.phong-shading.summary: An illumination model and shading technique that interpolates normals per pixel and sums ambient, diffuse, and specular terms.
a.poly1305.summary: A one-time MAC that produces a message authentication tag by polynomial evaluation over the prime field of order 2¹³⁰−5.
a.prim.o0.title: O jistém problému minimálním (letter to Borůvka)
a.prim.summary: A minimum spanning tree algorithm that starts from a single vertex and repeatedly adds the minimum-weight edge incident to the tree.
a.qhull.summary: A convex hull algorithm and implementation that generalizes Quickhull to arbitrary dimensions and is designed to handle numerical error.
a.quickhull.summary: A divide-and-conquer convex hull algorithm that splits the region at the farthest point, discards interior points, and recurses.
a.quickselect.summary: A selection algorithm that applies quicksort's partitioning recursively to only one side, finding the kth element in linear average time.
a.quicksort.o0.note: Detailed analysis in The Computer Journal 5(1), 1962
a.quicksort.summary: A divide-and-conquer sort that partitions the array around a pivot and recursively sorts both sides. It runs in O(n log n) average time and sorts in place.
a.r-tree.summary: A height-balanced tree that groups spatial objects by minimum bounding rectangles. It is the standard index for spatial databases.
a.rabin-karp.summary: A string search that finds pattern candidates by updating the hash of the text window in constant time with a rolling hash.
a.rader-fft.summary: An algorithm that converts a prime-length DFT into a cyclic convolution of length p−1 via a primitive-root permutation.
a.radix-sort.o0.note: Mechanical radix sorting on punched-card machines was in use earlier
a.radix-sort.summary: A non-comparison sort that repeatedly applies a stable sort digit by digit. The canonical form applies counting sort starting from the least significant digit (LSD).
a.raft.summary: A consensus algorithm designed for understandability by separating leader election, log replication, and safety.
a.random-forest.summary: An ensemble method that grows weakly correlated decision trees using bagged samples and random feature selection at each node, and combines them by voting.
a.random-subspace.summary: An ensemble method that trains a tree on each random subset of the features and combines the trees.
a.range-coding.summary: An entropy coding method that implements arithmetic coding with large integer ranges and byte-wise output.
a.ray-casting.summary: A rendering technique that casts a ray from the viewpoint through each pixel and determines visibility and shading from the first object hit.
a.red-black-tree.summary: A self-balancing binary search tree that colors each node red or black and uses coloring rules to keep the height O(log n).
a.reference-counting.summary: A memory management technique that counts the references to each object and reclaims it as soon as the count reaches zero.
a.rendezvous-hashing.summary: Highest random weight hashing, which selects the node whose key–node pair has the largest hash weight.
a.resnet.summary: An architecture that adds identity shortcut connections so that layers learn residual functions, making it possible to train networks with hundreds of layers.
a.rmsprop.summary: An adaptive optimizer that replaces the accumulated sum in AdaGrad with an exponential moving average, preventing the learning rate from decaying to zero.
a.robin-hood-hashing.summary: A linear-probing technique that makes keys yield their slots to keys displaced farther from their home positions, reducing the variance of probe lengths.
a.rope.summary: A positional encoding that rotates query and key vectors by angles proportional to position so that relative position appears in their dot product.
a.rsa.summary: A public-key encryption and digital signature scheme based on the assumed hardness of factoring large composite numbers.
a.salsa20.summary: A 20-round stream cipher built solely from addition, rotation, and XOR (ARX).
a.sbb-tree.summary: A balanced tree that represents a 2-3-4 B-tree as a binary tree. It is the direct predecessor of the red-black tree.
a.schnorr-signature.summary: A short, efficient signature obtained by applying the Fiat–Shamir transform to a discrete-logarithm-based identification protocol.
a.schonhage-strassen.summary: An algorithm that multiplies integers in O(n log n log log n) using a number-theoretic FFT over a ring of integers modulo a Fermat number.
a.scrypt.summary: A memory-hard key derivation function that uses the Salsa20/8 core and a large memory array.
a.seq2seq.summary: A neural machine translation architecture in which an encoder RNN summarizes the input sequence as a vector and a decoder RNN generates the output sequence.
a.sgd.summary: A stochastic approximation method for optimization that updates using the noisy gradient of a single sample or a minibatch instead of the full gradient.
a.sha-1.summary: A 160-bit hash that follows the design principles of MD4. A practical collision was published in 2017.
a.sha-2.summary: The SHA-224/256/384/512 family of hashes, using the Merkle–Damgård construction and a Davies–Meyer compression function.
a.sha-3.o0.title: Keccak (SHA-3 competition submission)
a.sha-3.summary: A hash that applies the sponge construction to the Keccak-f permutation. It is the winner of the NIST SHA-3 competition.
a.shadow-mapping.summary: A technique that renders a depth buffer from the light's viewpoint and then determines shadows by comparing each screen pixel's distance to the light against it.
a.shannon-fano.summary: A method that builds a prefix code by sorting symbols by probability and repeatedly splitting them into two groups of similar cumulative probability.
a.shellsort.summary: A sort that performs insertion sort on subsequences with decreasing gaps, moving elements long distances in a single step.
a.sieve-of-atkin.summary: A sieve that marks prime candidates by testing the number of solutions to quadratic forms.
a.sieve-of-eratosthenes.o0.title: As reported in Nicomachus, Introduction to Arithmetic
a.sieve-of-eratosthenes.summary: A sieve that finds all primes up to a bound by crossing out the multiples of each prime, starting from the smallest.
a.simplex-noise.summary: A gradient noise that uses a simplex lattice instead of a cubic lattice to reduce computation in higher dimensions.
a.simplex.o0.venue: In Activity Analysis of Production and Allocation (1951)
a.simplex.summary: A linear programming method that moves along the vertices of the feasible-region polytope in directions that improve the objective function.
a.simulated-annealing.summary: A global optimization method that explores solutions under the Metropolis acceptance rule while gradually lowering the temperature, allowing it to escape local optima.
a.skip-list.summary: A data structure that probabilistically promotes elements through multiple levels of linked lists, achieving expected O(log n) search.
a.smith-waterman.summary: A dynamic programming method that finds the most similar subsegments of two sequences (local alignment) by never letting scores fall below 0.
a.soft-margin-svm.summary: An extension that applies SVMs to data that is not linearly separable by allowing some misclassifications through slack variables.
a.spfa.summary: A queue-based improvement of Bellman–Ford that enqueues and relaxes only vertices whose distances have changed.
a.splay-tree.summary: A self-adjusting binary search tree that rotates each accessed node up to the root, achieving amortized O(log n) time.
a.sponge-construction.summary: A hash construction that handles arbitrary-length input and output by iterating a fixed permutation in two phases, absorbing and squeezing.
a.square-cipher.summary: An SPN block cipher whose diffusion is designed around byte-wise substitution and column mixing. It is the direct predecessor of Rijndael.
a.strassen-mm.summary: An algorithm that computes a 2×2 block product with seven multiplications, reducing matrix multiplication to O(n^2.807).
a.suffix-array.summary: An array of the starting positions of all suffixes of a string, sorted in lexicographic order. It uses less memory than a suffix tree.
a.suffix-automaton.summary: The minimal deterministic automaton that recognizes all substrings of a string. It has linear size and is built online.
a.suffix-tree.summary: A data structure that stores all suffixes of a string in a compressed trie, answering substring queries in time proportional to the pattern length.
a.svm.summary: A classifier that finds the hyperplane maximizing the margin between two classes and extends to nonlinear boundaries through kernels.
a.tarjan-scc.summary: An algorithm that finds the strongly connected components of a directed graph in linear time using a single DFS and low-link values.
a.timsort.o0.title: listsort.txt — CPython list.sort implementation
a.timsort.summary: An adaptive stable sort that finds already sorted segments (runs) in the input, extends them with binary insertion sort, and combines them with galloping merges.
a.toom-cook.summary: A generalization of Karatsuba that multiplies numbers by treating them as polynomials in k pieces, evaluating at several points, and interpolating.
a.topological-sort.summary: An algorithm that finds a topological order of a directed acyclic graph by repeatedly removing vertices with in-degree 0.
a.transformer.summary: A sequence model without recurrence that stacks scaled dot-product multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers with residual connections and normalization.
a.treap.summary: A probabilistically balanced tree that satisfies the binary search tree property on keys and the heap property on random priorities.
a.tri-color-marking.summary: A GC technique that partitions objects into white, gray, and black and maintains an invariant so that marking can proceed concurrently with the program.
a.trie.summary: A tree whose edges are the individual characters of strings. Sharing common prefixes makes prefix search fast.
a.two-phase-commit.summary: A protocol that guarantees atomicity of distributed transactions by having a coordinator collect prepare votes and then direct all participants to commit or abort together.
a.uct.summary: A Monte Carlo planning algorithm that balances exploration and exploitation at each tree node using the UCB1 bandit formula.
a.ukkonen-algorithm.summary: An algorithm that builds a suffix tree online in linear time, reading characters one at a time from left to right.
a.union-find.summary: A data structure that represents elements as trees of disjoint sets, performing union and find-representative operations in nearly constant time.
a.vector-clock.summary: A logical clock that uses a vector of per-process counters to determine causality and concurrency between events exactly.
a.vgg.summary: A convolutional neural network built by deeply stacking only 3×3 convolutions, demonstrating the effect of depth on performance.
a.viewstamped-replication.summary: A fault-tolerant state machine replication scheme based on a primary replica and a view-change protocol.
a.viterbi.summary: An algorithm that uses dynamic programming to find the hidden state sequence of a hidden Markov model that best explains an observation sequence.
a.wagner-fischer.summary: An algorithm that computes a generalized edit distance in O(nm) using a dynamic programming table over pairs of prefixes of the two strings.
a.wave-function-collapse.summary: A procedural generation algorithm that generates tilemaps and levels by fixing cells, lowest-entropy first, and propagating local pattern constraints taken from an example image.
a.whitted-ray-tracing.summary: A ray tracing method that recursively traces reflection, refraction, and shadow rays from each intersection point.
a.xgboost.summary: Scalable gradient boosting that adds a second-order approximation of the objective, regularization, sparsity-aware split finding, and cache optimization.
a.xiaolin-wu-line.summary: An antialiased line algorithm that divides intensity, in proportion to distance, between the two pixels the line straddles.
a.xorshift.summary: A family of very fast pseudorandom number generators that update their state using only shifts and XORs.
a.xoshiro.summary: A family of pseudorandom number generators that improves on xorshift's statistical quality by adding rotations and an output scrambler.
a.z-buffer.summary: A hidden-surface removal technique that stores the nearest depth value for each pixel to eliminate occluded surfaces pixel by pixel.
a.zstd.summary: A compression method that encodes LZ77 matches with tANS (FSE) and Huffman codes. It offers a wide range of speeds and compression ratios.
e.a-star>d-star: Named as a dynamic A* for environments with changing costs
e.a-star>ida-star: Presented as iterative deepening on A*'s f-value bound
e.a-star>jump-point-search: Presented as pruning that reduces the nodes A* expands to jump points
e.adaboost>gradient-boosting: Interprets AdaBoost as a stagewise additive model and generalizes it to arbitrary losses
e.adagrad>adam: The Adam paper states that it combines the advantages of AdaGrad and RMSProp
e.adagrad>rmsprop: Replaces AdaGrad's accumulated sum of squares with a moving average (Adam paper, related work section)
e.adam>adamw: Presents a modification of Adam with decoupled weight decay
e.additive-attention>dot-product-attenti: Proposes a simpler scoring function, compared against Bahdanau attention
e.alexnet>vgg: Increases depth, taking the configuration of Krizhevsky et al. as the baseline
e.ans>zstd: The FSE of RFC 8878 is a tANS implementation
e.arithmetic-coding>ans: Duda presented it as achieving both the compression ratio of arithmetic coding and the speed of Huffman coding
e.arithmetic-coding>range-coding: Equivalent scheme that implements arithmetic coding with integer ranges and byte-wise output
e.b-tree>lsm-tree: The LSM paper compares write costs with B-trees, but there is no derivation relationship
e.b-tree>r-tree: Describes the R-tree as a height-balanced tree similar to the B-tree
e.b-tree>sbb-tree: Bayer presented it as a binary-tree representation of B-trees
e.backpropagation>lenet: As the paper's title says, applies backpropagation to training a convolutional neural network
e.bagging>random-forest: States that it combines bagging with random feature selection
e.batch-norm>layer-norm: Presented as batch normalization moved from the batch dimension to the layer dimension
e.batch-norm>resnet: States that batch normalization is applied after each convolution
e.baum-welch>em: Dempster et al. cite the HMM estimation of Baum et al. as an instance of EM
e.bellman-ford>johnson: Computes potentials with Bellman–Ford to reweight edges
e.bellman-ford>spfa: Queue-based improvement of Bellman–Ford that re-relaxes only updated vertices (the same idea appears in Moore 1959)
e.bentley-ottmann>fortune: Applies the same plane-sweep technique to a different problem
e.bfs>dijkstra: With all weights equal it visits vertices in the same order as BFS, but no evidence that it originated from BFS
e.bfs>edmonds-karp: Finds shortest augmenting paths with BFS (CLRS §26.2)
e.binary-heap>binomial-heap: Generalizes heap-ordered trees to a forest as a mergeable priority queue
e.binary-heap>heapsort: Williams's Algorithm 232 defines the heap data structure and presents a sort that uses it
e.binary-heap>treap: By definition, priorities satisfy heap order
e.binary-insertion-sort>timsort: listsort.txt describes extending short runs to the minimum length with binary insertion sort
e.binary-search>exponential-search: The Bentley–Yao algorithm finds an upper bound exponentially, then performs binary search
e.binary-search>interpolation-search: Chooses the probe position by interpolating key values instead of taking the midpoint (treated together in Knuth TAOCP Vol.3 §6.2.1)
e.binomial-heap>fibonacci-heap: Defines Fibonacci heaps as binomial queues with lazily deferred operations
e.binomial-heap>pairing-heap: Self-adjusting heap that simplifies binomial-heap merging to pairing within a single tree
e.bitonic-sort>odd-even-merge-sort: Sorting networks presented together in the same paper; neither derives from the other
e.blake2>argon2: RFC 9106 uses BLAKE2b as Argon2's hash function
e.blake2>blake3: The BLAKE3 specification states that it reuses the BLAKE2s compression function with reduced rounds
e.blake>blake2: Presented as an improvement of BLAKE with fewer rounds and an added parameter block
e.bloom-filter>count-min-sketch: Similar structure of marking array cells with multiple hashes, but no evidence of derivation
e.bloom-filter>counting-bloom-filter: Fan et al. extend Bloom filter bits to counters to support deletion
e.bloom-filter>cuckoo-filter: Compared as a replacement for Bloom filters, but not derived from them
e.blowfish>bcrypt: Defines Eksblowfish, which repeats the Blowfish key schedule according to a cost factor
e.boruvka>kruskal: Addresses the same minimum spanning tree problem, but no evidence of derivation
e.boruvka>prim: Jarník's 1930 manuscript was a letter to Borůvka solving the same problem in a different way
e.boyer-moore>horspool: Presented as a simplification that keeps only Boyer–Moore's bad-character rule
e.bresenham-line>bresenham-circle: The same author extends incremental integer rasterization to circular arcs
e.bresenham-line>xiaolin-wu-line: Adds pixel intensity distribution to the same incremental line rasterization
e.bst>avl-tree: The first self-balancing tree, adding a height-balance condition to the binary search tree (Knuth TAOCP Vol.3 §6.2.3)
e.bst>kd-tree: As the paper's title says, generalizes binary search trees to multiple dimensions
e.bst>skip-list: Presented as an alternative to balanced trees, but not derived from trees
e.bst>splay-tree: Defined as a binary search tree that self-adjusts via rotations
e.bst>treap: By definition, keys satisfy binary search tree order (the name is tree + heap)
e.bwt>bzip2: Uses the Burrows–Wheeler transform as the block-sorting stage
e.bwt>fm-index: Compressed index that adds rank-query structures on top of the BWT
e.cart>gradient-boosting: Uses regression trees as weak learners
e.cart>id3: Decision tree induction methods developed independently around the same time
e.chacha>blake: The BLAKE proposal states that its compression function core uses a modified ChaCha
e.chacha>chacha20-poly1305: RFC 7539 defines the AEAD combination of ChaCha20 and Poly1305
e.cheney>generational-gc: Ungar's generation scavenging uses copying collection for the young generation
e.consistent-hashing>chord: States that it uses consistent hashing to assign nodes and keys
e.consistent-hashing>jump-consistent-has: Presented as achieving the same properties as consistent hashing without storage
e.consistent-hashing>rendezvous-hashing: Solves the same distributed assignment problem in a different way
e.copying-gc>cheney: Presents a way to perform copying GC without recursion
e.counting-sort>radix-sort: LSD radix sort applies a stable counting sort to each digit (CLRS §8.3)
e.cuckoo-hashing>cuckoo-filter: The paper describes storing fingerprints with partial-key cuckoo hashing
e.cyk>earley: Solves the same general context-free parsing problem with a chart-based approach
e.dfs>ida-star: Each iteration is a depth-first search within the f-value bound
e.dfs>kosaraju-scc: Applies DFS twice, to the original graph and to its transpose (CLRS §22.5)
e.dfs>tarjan-scc: The paper's title and body state that it is based on depth-first search
e.dfs>topological-sort: DFS finishing order also yields a topological sort, but Kahn's method is based on in-degrees
e.diffie-hellman>ecc: Miller proposed carrying Diffie–Hellman key exchange over to elliptic curve groups
e.diffie-hellman>elgamal: Presented as public-key encryption and signatures based on the Diffie–Hellman key distribution scheme
e.diffie-hellman>rsa: Realizes the public-key concept proposed by Diffie and Hellman under a different mathematical assumption
e.dijkstra>a-star: A* with heuristic h = 0 is identical to Dijkstra (Russell and Norvig, AIMA)
e.dijkstra>johnson: Runs Dijkstra from each vertex after reweighting
e.dinic>edmonds-karp: Improvements based on shortest augmenting paths, published independently of each other
e.dot-product-attention>transformer: States that it is identical to dot-product attention except for the scaling factor
e.dropout>alexnet: States that dropout is used in the fully connected layers
e.dropout>transformer: States that dropout is applied to the output of each sub-layer
e.dsa>ecdsa: Signature scheme that carries DSA over to elliptic curve groups
e.ecc>eddsa: Uses twisted Edwards curve group operations
e.elgamal>dsa: Described as a variant of ElGamal signatures (Menezes et al., Handbook of Applied Cryptography §11.5)
e.elgamal>schnorr-signature: A later scheme in the discrete-log signature family, but no explicit statement of direct derivation found
e.fft>bluestein-fft: Computes arbitrary-length DFTs via convolutions using power-of-two FFTs
e.fft>rader-fft: Computes prime-length DFTs via FFT-based cyclic convolution
e.fft>schonhage-strassen: Computes the convolution with a number-theoretic FFT
e.flajolet-martin>loglog: Follow-up work by the same author (Flajolet) that changes the observable to reduce memory
e.flash-attention>flash-attention-2: Successor that improves FlashAttention's work partitioning
e.ford-fulkerson>dinic: Batches the augmenting-path method using level graphs and blocking flows
e.ford-fulkerson>edmonds-karp: Improvement of Ford–Fulkerson that chooses shortest paths as augmenting paths
e.furer>harvey-van-der-hoeven: Cites the line of improvements following Fürer and reaches O(n log n)
e.gouraud-shading>phong-shading: Phong interpolates normals instead of vertex intensities, fixing the loss of highlights in Gouraud shading
e.gradient-boosting>lightgbm: Improves GBDT training efficiency with GOSS and EFB
e.gradient-boosting>xgboost: Presented as a scalable implementation of gradient tree boosting
e.gradient-descent>momentum: Proposes adding an inertia term to gradient methods to accelerate convergence
e.gradient-descent>sgd: Gradient descent with the full gradient replaced by a stochastic estimate (Robbins–Monro stochastic approximation is the theoretical basis)
e.graham-scan>chan-hull: Combines per-group Graham scans with a Jarvis march
e.graham-scan>monotone-chain: Described as a Graham scan variant that sorts by x-coordinate instead of polar angle
e.hash-chaining>linear-probing: Same hash table with collision resolution switched from chaining to open addressing (Knuth TAOCP Vol.3 §6.4)
e.heapsort>introsort: Ranges that exceed the recursion depth limit are handled by heapsort
e.hmac>pbkdf2: RFC 2898 specifies HMAC-SHA-1 as the underlying pseudorandom function
e.huffman>brotli: RFC 7932 defines it as a combination of LZ77, Huffman coding, and second-order context modeling
e.huffman>bzip2: Uses Huffman coding as the final entropy stage
e.huffman>deflate: RFC 1951 defines Deflate as a combination of LZ77 and Huffman coding
e.huffman>zstd: RFC 8878 compresses literals with Huffman coding
e.hunt-szymanski>myers-diff: A different approach to the same LCS/diff problem
e.hyperloglog>hyperloglog-pp: Presented as a practical improvement of HyperLogLog
e.id3>c4-5: Published by Quinlan as the successor to ID3
e.insertion-sort>binary-insertion-sort: Replaces only the insertion-point search with binary search; described in Knuth TAOCP Vol.3 §5.2.1
e.insertion-sort>shellsort: Shell presented it as a diminishing-increment method that performs insertion sort for each gap
e.introsort>pdqsort: The paper introduces pdqsort as an extension of introsort
e.jarvis-march>chan-hull: Combines per-group Graham scans with a Jarvis march
e.k-means>em: k-means can be interpreted as the hard-assignment limit of EM, but was historically devised first
e.k-means>k-means-pp: Presented as a method that changes only how k-means chooses its initial centers
e.karatsuba>toom-cook: Karatsuba is the special case of Toom–Cook with two pieces (Knuth TAOCP Vol.2 §4.3.3)
e.kmp>aho-corasick: Generalizes the KMP failure function to a trie of the pattern set (standard textbook account)
e.kmp>boyer-moore: Contemporary linear-time single-pattern search, but based on a different principle
e.lamport-clock>vector-clock: Generalizes Lamport's logical clock to per-process vectors
e.layer-norm>transformer: Applies layer normalization after the residual connection, citing Ba et al.
e.lcg>pcg: States that it combines LCG state transitions with a permutation output function
e.lenet>alexnet: Cites LeCun's line of convolutional neural networks and scales up depth and size
e.levenshtein-distance>wagner-fischer: Computes Levenshtein distance by dynamic programming and generalizes edit costs (the same DP was discovered independently by several researchers)
e.linear-probing>cuckoo-hashing: Within the open-addressing family, fixes the candidate locations to two hashes and allows relocation
e.linear-probing>robin-hood-hashing: Celis et al. presented it as an insertion rule that reduces the variance of probe lengths in open addressing
e.loglog>hyperloglog: Described as combining LogLog registers with a harmonic mean to reduce error
e.lr-parsing>lalr: Presents a way to reduce Knuth's LR(k) parsers to a practical size
e.lstm>gru: Proposes a simpler gated unit motivated by the LSTM
e.lstm>seq2seq: Sutskever et al. use multilayer LSTMs for the encoder and decoder
e.lucifer>des: Standardized as a modification of IBM's Lucifer
e.lz77>brotli: RFC 7932 defines it as a combination of LZ77, Huffman coding, and second-order context modeling
e.lz77>deflate: RFC 1951 defines Deflate as a combination of LZ77 and Huffman coding
e.lz77>lz4: Byte-oriented LZ77-family format with no entropy stage
e.lz77>lzma: Range-codes the output of LZ77-style match finding
e.lz77>lzss: LZ77 improvement that emits short matches as literals
e.lz77>zstd: RFC 8878 defines LZ77-style sequences and FSE/Huffman entropy stages
e.lz78>lzw: Initializes the dictionary with all single characters, eliminating LZ78's literal output
e.mark-sweep>copying-gc: Tracing GC that reclaims by copying instead of sweeping
e.mark-sweep>tri-color-marking: Presents a way to run the marking phase concurrently with the mutator
e.mccreight-algorithm>ukkonen-algorithm: Giegerich and Kurtz (1997) showed the two constructions share the same suffix-link principle, but neither derives from the other
e.mcts>uct: Monte Carlo tree search methods published independently in the same year
e.md4>md5: RFC 1321 describes MD5 as an extension of MD4
e.md4>sha-1: Follows the same design principles as MD4 (Handbook of Applied Cryptography §9.4)
e.merge-sort>odd-even-merge-sort: Carries the recursive structure of merge sort over to a fixed comparator network
e.merge-sort>timsort: listsort.txt describes run-based merging and galloping merges as its core
e.merkle-damgard>md4: Iterated hash structure that chains a compression function over each block (Handbook of Applied Cryptography §9.4)
e.merkle-damgard>sha-2: Uses a Davies–Meyer compression function within the Merkle–Damgård construction
e.merkle-tree>blake3: The BLAKE3 specification states that input is hashed as a binary Merkle tree of chunks
e.metropolis-hastings>gibbs-sampling: Can be interpreted as a special case of MH with acceptance probability 1, but was proposed independently
e.metropolis>metropolis-hastings: Generalizes the Metropolis method to asymmetric proposal distributions
e.metropolis>simulated-annealing: Presented as the Metropolis algorithm with an added temperature schedule
e.minimax>alpha-beta: Yields the same value as minimax while pruning unnecessary branches (analysis by Knuth and Moore, 1975)
e.minimax>mcts: Approaches the same game tree search problem through sampling
e.momentum>adam: The first-moment moving average plays the same role as the momentum term
e.momentum>nesterov: Accelerated variant that evaluates the gradient at the point reached after the momentum step
e.monte-carlo>mcts: Estimates node values as Monte Carlo averages over random playouts
e.monte-carlo>metropolis: Extends random sampling to Markov chains (Metropolis is a shared author)
e.monte-carlo>path-tracing: Computes the rendering equation via Monte Carlo integration over random path samples
e.move-to-front>bzip2: Applies the MTF transform to the BWT output
e.multi-query-attention>grouped-query-at: Defined as a generalization of multi-query attention
e.needleman-wunsch>smith-waterman: Modifies global-alignment dynamic programming for local alignment
e.needleman-wunsch>wagner-fischer: The same form of dynamic programming was published independently in biology and in computer science
e.neocognitron>lenet: Papers in the convolutional neural network line cite the neocognitron as prior work
e.pagerank>hits: Link analysis algorithms proposed independently around the same time
e.paxos>raft: Designed as an understandable alternative equivalent to (Multi-)Paxos
e.pbkdf2>scrypt: Uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 in the input and output stages
e.perceptron>backpropagation: Solved the problem of training multilayer perceptrons, but is not derived from the perceptron learning rule
e.perceptron>svm: Addresses the same problem of learning a linearly separating hyperplane
e.perlin-noise>improved-perlin-noise: The same author improves the original noise's interpolation function and gradient selection
e.perlin-noise>simplex-noise: Presented by the same author as a successor noise that replaces the lattice with a simplex lattice
e.phong-shading>blinn-phong: Blinn presented a variant that recasts the Phong model's specular term in terms of the halfway vector
e.poly1305>chacha20-poly1305: RFC 7539 defines the AEAD combination of ChaCha20 and Poly1305
e.quickselect>median-of-medians: Replacing pivot selection with the median of medians improves the worst case from O(n²) to O(n) (CLRS §9.3)
e.quicksort>dual-pivot-quicksort: Quicksort with single-pivot partitioning replaced by three-way partitioning around two pivots
e.quicksort>introsort: Musser defined it as starting with quicksort and switching to heapsort once the recursion depth limit is exceeded
e.quicksort>quickhull: Named for a divide-and-conquer structure resembling quicksort, but no evidence of derivation
e.quicksort>quickselect: Published together by the same author in the same issue (CACM 4(7)) as Algorithms 63, 64, and 65, which share the partition procedure
e.random-subspace>random-forest: Cites Ho's random subspace method as prior work
e.range-coding>lzma: Uses context-model-based range coding as the entropy stage
e.ray-casting>whitted-ray-tracing: Extends primary ray casting to recursive tracing of reflection, refraction, and shadow rays
e.red-black-tree>aa-tree: Andersson presented it as a simplified variant of red-black trees requiring less case analysis
e.resnet>transformer: Uses a residual connection around each sub-layer, citing He et al.
e.rmsprop>adam: The Adam paper states that it combines the advantages of AdaGrad and RMSProp
e.salsa20>chacha: The ChaCha document is titled "a variant of Salsa20"
e.salsa20>scrypt: Uses the Salsa20/8 core in BlockMix
e.sbb-tree>red-black-tree: The dichromatic framework reformulates symmetric binary B-trees in terms of color rules
e.schnorr-signature>dsa: Structural similarity led to a patent dispute, but no official statement of derivation
e.schnorr-signature>eddsa: Describes EdDSA as a variant of Schnorr signatures
e.schonhage-strassen>furer: States that it improves on the Schönhage–Strassen bound
e.seq2seq>additive-attention: Identifies the fixed-length vector bottleneck and extends the encoder–decoder to learn alignment
e.sgd>adagrad: Introduces per-coordinate adaptive learning rates into stochastic (sub)gradient updates
e.sha-1>sha-2: Extends the word size and round functions within the same FIPS 180 family
e.shannon-fano>huffman: Optimal prefix code that originated as an assignment in Fano's course and resolved the suboptimality of Shannon–Fano coding
e.sieve-of-eratosthenes>linear-sieve: Presented as a linear-time sieve that crosses out each composite only once
e.sieve-of-eratosthenes>sieve-of-atkin: Compared with the sieve of Eratosthenes, but uses a different principle based on quadratic forms
e.simplex>karmarkar: A separate method that solves the same linear programming problem by an interior-point approach
e.smith-waterman>blast: Approximates local alignment with a word-seed extension heuristic to gain speed
e.splay-tree>pairing-heap: Same group of authors (Sleator, Tarjan) applies self-adjusting amortized analysis to heaps
e.sponge-construction>sha-3: Defines Keccak as a sponge function over the Keccak-f permutation
e.square-cipher>aes: The Rijndael proposal states that it is a successor design to Square
e.strassen-mm>coppersmith-winograd: A later result in the line of work, following Strassen, that lowers the matrix multiplication exponent
e.suffix-array>fm-index: The BWT column is defined by suffix array order, and locate queries use a sampled suffix array
e.suffix-tree>mccreight-algorithm: Presented as a more space-efficient suffix tree construction than Weiner's
e.suffix-tree>suffix-array: Manber and Myers presented it as an alternative that uses less space than suffix trees
e.suffix-tree>suffix-automaton: Support the same substring queries and correspond to each other, but no evidence of derivation
e.suffix-tree>ukkonen-algorithm: Presented as an online, left-to-right construction of suffix trees
e.svm>soft-margin-svm: Extends the optimal margin classifier to the non-separable case
e.transformer>bert: States that it is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder
e.transformer>flash-attention: Presented as an IO-aware implementation that produces the same results as standard attention
e.transformer>gpt: States that it uses a multi-layer Transformer decoder
e.transformer>lora: Mainly applied to Transformer weights, but not a technique derived from the architecture
e.transformer>multi-query-attention: Proposes a variant of multi-head attention in which the key and value heads are shared as a single head
e.transformer>rope: Replaces the Transformer's positional encoding with rotation matrices
e.trie>aho-corasick: Automaton that adds a failure function to the pattern-set trie (goto function)
e.trie>patricia-trie: Trie with single-child paths compressed (Knuth TAOCP Vol.3 §6.3)
e.trie>suffix-tree: Defined as a compressed trie of all suffixes
e.vgg>resnet: States that the plain baseline network is inspired by the philosophy of VGG
e.viewstamped-replication>paxos: Replicated consensus schemes devised independently around the same time
e.viewstamped-replication>raft: The Raft paper states that, of existing algorithms, it is most similar to Viewstamped Replication
e.viterbi>baum-welch: Both use dynamic programming over the same HMM trellis, but for different purposes
e.wagner-fischer>myers-diff: Finds the shortest edit script on the edit graph in time proportional to the number of differences D
e.whitted-ray-tracing>path-tracing: Kajiya recast existing ray tracing methods as special approximations of the rendering equation and generalized them
e.xorshift>xoshiro: Adds a scrambler to the xorshift-family linear engine
e.z-buffer>shadow-mapping: Uses a depth buffer rendered from the light's viewpoint for shadow tests
